fact_check.claim: Gas-heat household pays about $241 a month during the Nov-Mar heating season in 2026-27, based on 140 therms
fact_check.note: Page: 'estimated $241 per month during the winter heating season (November through March)'; 2026-27 season named in the forecast intro.

fact_check.claim: Electric: 600 kWh a month, about $74 a month for supply, up 4.6% from a year earlier
fact_check.note: Page says about $74 per month for supply, up 4.6%; amounts vary by utility.

fact_check.claim: Natural gas about $241 a month, down 3.2%
fact_check.note: Page says down 3.2% from a year earlier.

fact_check.claim: Supply is roughly 35 to 45% of a bill
fact_check.note: Page: roughly 35-45%, depending on local utility.

fact_check.claim: A colder-than-normal winter raises usage and bills
fact_check.note: Page: 'A colder-than-normal winter will cause usage and bills to increase.'

fact_check.claim: State recommends 68 degrees while home and lower when away or asleep
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: State suggests sealing drafts around windows and doors and opening curtains on sunny winter days
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Balanced billing spreads costs evenly across the year; lowers monthly swings but not annual total
fact_check.note: Page: equal monthly payments, does not lower annual total.

fact_check.claim: Cold Weather Rules run November 1 to April 15
fact_check.note: Dates match. The article's description of the rule (utilities must make a special effort to check health or safety harm before shutting off heat service) was not separately confirmed in the extract but the dates are right.

fact_check.claim: NYSEG holiday pause December 22, 2025 to January 2, 2026 (2026-27 dates not posted)
fact_check.note: Page lists those dates for 2025-26 and says to check for updated dates.
Matches HEAP hotline on page.

fact_check.claim: Ithaca electricity about 25 cents per kWh
fact_check.note: $0.25/kWh, about 16% above national average.

fact_check.claim: EnergySage Ithaca average about $280 a month on about 1,116 kWh, updated November 1, 2026
fact_check.note: Matches, including update date.

fact_check.claim: Figures come from residents who requested quotes; solar shoppers may use more electricity than typical
fact_check.note: Page says so.

fact_check.claim: Ithaca College: 65 degree daytime setting can cut heating use by as much as 15%; 58 degrees before winter break
fact_check.note: Matches the Off-Campus & Circle Apartment section; page does not state the unit but degrees F is implied.

fact_check.claim: Cornell neighborhoods page: lakeside areas northwest of the city, 'cottages' probably not insulated, houses probably are, winter heating bills 'can be astronomical'
fact_check.note: West Hill entry says this. Short quoted phrases only.

fact_check.claim: Cornell tells renters to check with NYSEG, which has a listed phone number there, for average yearly heating bills
fact_check.note: Page lists NYSEG at (800) 572-1111. Article could print it.

fact_check.claim: Cornell checklist: include utilities when calculating maximum affordable rent; arrange utilities on by move-in
fact_check.note: Both sentences are on the page.

fact_check.claim: Several recent threads on other New York subreddits describe resistance electric heat as the costly option
fact_check.note: No source link; the article admits it could not open the threads. An unverifiable claim about sources not read must not be published.

fact_check.claim: Some listings advertise utilities included (FAQ)
fact_check.note: No source link. Search shows apartment listings with utilities included in Ithaca, but the article cites none.

fact_check.claim: State figures are 'a ceiling check, not a promise'; a one-bedroom shared by two will use far less than 140 therms, a poorly insulated four-roommate house could use more
fact_check.note: Not supported by the source; the state page gives no ceiling and no per-apartment usage. Presented as fact with no basis, and self-contradictory (ceiling, then 'could use more').

beats_top.query: ithaca utilities cost winter heating bill apartment students
beats_top.why: The #1 result is an Ithaca College thermostat-tips page with no dollar figures, so our page is already more useful. But the planned angle was ranges by heat type, and ours gives none: a student still has no usable monthly estimate for their own unit.
changes: Add a worked, labeled estimate for electric-heat and gas-heat units from the sourced inputs (for example 1,116 kWh x $0.25 = about $280, and the $74 supply and $241 gas state forecasts), clearly marked as illustrative, with the sources linked and the per-roommate split shown.
Print the NYSEG number from the Cornell page, (800) 572-1111, in the landlord/average-bills section.
Remove claims that have no source (Reddit, 'ceiling check', FAQ utilities-included) so the lead no longer disclaims its own numbers.

fixes: Delete the paragraph beginning 'Several recent threads on other New York subreddits' (no source; the article admits it could not open them). If the point about resistance electric heat is kept, phrase it only as a question to ask the landlord, with no claim about what others say.

In the FAQ answer 'Is heat usually included in Ithaca student rent?', remove 'Some listings advertise utilities included' or link a specific Ithaca listing page that shows it (for example https://www.apartmentfinder.com/New-York/East-Ithaca-Apartments-With-Utilities-Included); keep 'ask and get it in the lease'.

In 'What the official numbers say', delete 'They are a ceiling check, not a promise.' and the sentences saying a shared one-bedroom 'will use far less than 140 therms' and a four-roommate house 'could use more'; replace with: 'These are statewide forecasts for a typical household; the state says actual amounts vary by utility and region.' (source https://dps.ny.gov/winter).

Add the NYSEG phone number (800) 572-1111 to the 'Older houses and lakeside rentals' paragraph and the FAQ answer 'Who do I call for average bills?', linking https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/housing-search-process/ithaca-neighborhoods.

Add a short 'Rough monthly arithmetic' section after the heat-type table giving winter ranges by heat type using only sourced inputs: electric (EnergySage 1,116 kWh x $0.25 = about $280/month, noting its sample bias and that this includes delivery), and gas heat (state forecast $241/month at 140 therms plus the $74 electric supply forecast). Label as illustrative, not Ithaca student-apartment data, and show the split by 2, 3 and 4 roommates as simple division. Do not invent summer figures; keep 'we found no Ithaca-specific figure' for winter vs summer.
Rewrite the first paragraph so the first sentence gives the usable answer (the sourced numbers and what to do) instead of opening with 'any single number you see online is a guess, including ours'.
